clue.text: Soft money in Sofia reflected on screen

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the other way round, so the Bulgarian currency is read backwards

parts.note: the lev is the currency of Bulgaria, whose capital is Sofia
to vet is to screen or check someone

explanation.surface: Bulgarian cash appears in a film or on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' reverses the Bulgarian currency; 'on' just places that ahead of the second piece. 'Soft' is an adjective here, as in velvet tones.
explanation.definitionFit: Velvet is a byword for softness, used as an adjective for something smooth and soft.

clue.text: Confirm correctness of Delia, a TV cook

indicators.note: to cook figures is to fiddle them, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Delia Smith, a TV chef, is endorsed as getting things right.
explanation.walkthrough: Delia Smith is a famous British television cook, which makes 'cook' look like a noun; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To validate something is to check and confirm that it is sound or correct.

clue.text: East Anglia's foremost player exchanged in 2012, say

indicators.note: the letters swap places with each other, so they are rearranged
the foremost letters of East and Anglia's are taken, their first letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sportsman from eastern England was transferred to another club in 2012.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanged' shuffles EA (the first letters of East and Anglia's) with PLAYER to make the answer; 2012 had a 29 February.
explanation.definitionFit: 2012 was a year with 366 days, an example of the four-yearly calendar adjustment.

clue.text: Guarantee nurse dissipated energy

indicators.note: dissipated means scattered, so the letters of nurse are scattered

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A nurse's guaranteed energy has drained away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dissipated' rearranges NURSE into ENSUR, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure something is to make certain of it, the verb sense of guarantee.

clue.text: Turkey's accompaniment — overturned bottle bottling nasty smell

indicators.note: turned upside down, so in an across clue the whole construction is read backwards
bottling means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: bottle is British slang for courage, as is guts
niff is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A bottle has tipped over at Christmas dinner and released a foul smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reverses the whole container, giving GNIFFUTS backwards. Niff is British slang for a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffing is the seasoned filling traditionally served with roast turkey.

clue.text: Elevated ingredient of gin

indicators.note: raised up, so in a down clue the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an ingredient is a part of a mixture

explanation.surface: A raised component of a gin drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' looks like the spirit, but it is a snare for catching animals; 'Elevated' turns PART upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is an old word for a snare used to catch game, the same thing as a trap.

clue.text: Parting of the ways, when turning in two directions, abandoned

indicators.note: the reversed word is placed in the parting of the ways

parts.note: a fork is where a road divides

indicators.note: turning means going back on itself, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
E and N are the compass points east and north

explanation.surface: Lovers split up and went separate ways and were left alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes the reversed SA, and 'in' sets it inside; 'two directions' are compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsaken means deserted or left behind, a synonym of abandoned.

clue.text: Artist's endless entrance

definitions.note: read as 'artist is', a noun naming the painter

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: ingress is a formal word for entry or entrance

explanation.surface: A painter's never-ending entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' takes the last S off INGRESS. Ingres was a French Neoclassical painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French painter, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Expression of surprise about a left shoe

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the exclamation goes round the other letters

parts.note: gosh is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at finding a single shoe abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places GOSH around A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A galosh is a rubber overshoe worn to keep ordinary shoes dry.

clue.text: Foster co-operation with tall tale about sloths

indicators.note: about means around, so the untruth is wrapped round the animals

parts.note: a tall tale is a lie
an ai is a three-toed sloth, so ais are sloths

explanation.surface: Encouraging teamwork by telling an exaggerated story about lazy animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Ai is a crossword favourite for the three-toed sloth; 'tall tale' is not an anagram cue, simply a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to act as a link between groups, working together and encouraging cooperation.

clue.text: Capital curtailed lass's song

indicators.note: curtailed means shortened at the tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Madrid is the capital city of Spain
a gal is a lass or girl

explanation.surface: A girl's song is cut short in a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' takes the final D from MADRID; the 's of lass's links.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a part song for several unaccompanied voices, popular in the Renaissance.

clue.text: Ray maybe getting silly hat encrypted?

indicators.note: the code word gets, or takes in, the rearranged letters

parts.note: something encrypted is put into code

indicators.note: silly means foolish or muddled, so the letters of hat are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man called Ray is given a silly hat in a secret message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' makes ATH; 'getting' takes it inside. 'Ray' looks like a man's name; it is a beam of electrons.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathode ray is a stream of electrons, so the electrode names a kind of ray.

clue.text: 24 hours off dawn?

parts.note: a day lasts twenty-four hours
time off is a break

explanation.surface: Taking a whole day off at first light.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful split: a day plus a break means a day off.
explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak is the first light of morning, the same as dawn.

clue.text: Worries about second stroke

parts.note: cares are worries or anxieties

explanation.surface: Anxieties about a second attack of illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stroke' looks like a medical event, but it is a gentle touch.
explanation.definitionFit: To caress is to stroke someone affectionately, so both name a light, loving touch.

clue.text: Pub sign put up outside, one with a girl in play

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the reversed sign goes round the pub
put up means raised, so in a down clue the star sign reads upwards

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
PH is the map abbreviation for public house
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A pub sign is hung up outside, and a man with a girl goes to the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' gives OEL upwards, and 'outside' wraps that round the pub abbreviation. PH is a British map abbreviation for a public house.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophelia is the young woman in Shakespeare's Hamlet who drowns herself.

clue.text: Cut head off wood

indicators.note: taking the head off removes the first letter

parts.note: a steak is a cut of meat

explanation.surface: A tree is chopped down by cutting off its top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' takes the first letter S from STEAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Teak is a hard tropical timber prized for furniture and boats.

clue.text: Woodcutter, perhaps, in good spirits

definitions.meaning: a machine or person that chips wood, an example of something that cuts wood

explanation.definitionFit: A wood chipper cuts timber into chips; chipper is also an informal word for cheerful.

clue.text: Wheedle, being rather tasteless?

parts.note: bland food has little taste
the suffix -ish means rather or somewhat

explanation.surface: Coaxing someone in a rather insipid way.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the split reading of the answer as 'somewhat bland'.
explanation.definitionFit: To blandish is to coax someone with flattery, which is what wheedling means.

clue.text: Discard a large body of water with two ears

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it away
the Ural is a long river running from Russia into the Caspian Sea

explanation.surface: Throwing away a great expanse of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Binaural means relating to both ears, as in sound recorded for two-eared listening.

clue.text: Passenger's support heartlessly shattered — shattered!

indicators.note: shattered means broken into pieces, so the letters are rearranged
without its heart, so the central letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: A car seat's head support is broken, and its owner is exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' takes the middle T from SHATTERED, leaving SHATERED, and the second 'shattered' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: A headrest is the cushion behind a car passenger's head, supporting it.

clue.text: Run after introduction to barrel organ

indicators.note: after places the run behind the first letter
the introduction to a word is its first letter

parts.note: a ladder is a run in tights or stockings

explanation.surface: A tune follows the opening of a barrel organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests music after 'barrel organ', but it is a body part. A ladder is the British word for a run in tights.
explanation.definitionFit: The bladder is the organ of the body that stores urine.

clue.text: Deputy's bad habit

definitions.meaning: read as 'deputy is': a second in command

explanation.definitionFit: Vice is a prefix meaning deputy, and as a noun it is a moral failing or bad habit.

clue.text: Tread carefully, exchanging Spain for Portugal? Splendid!

indicators.note: exchanging one thing for another replaces one letter with the other

parts.note: to tiptoe is to walk quietly and carefully
E is the international vehicle code for Spain
P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: Walking carefully across the Iberian border is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanging' swaps the E at the end of TIPTOE for P.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip-top is an informal word meaning excellent or first-rate.

clue.text: "Terminator" is nearer the mark

definitions.meaning: something that ends or finishes, like a final item in a show

explanation.definitionFit: A closer is the last act or item that ends something, and the comparative of close means nearer.

clue.text: I see 5 captured by media company's servant

indicators.note: captured by means held inside, so the letters go within the company name

parts.note: Sky is a British broadcasting company
V stands for vide, Latin for see
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's camera captures a domestic worker.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British satellite TV company. Skivvy is British slang for a lowly domestic servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A skivvy is a menial domestic servant, a British informal term.

clue.text: One nation incorporating Sweden and Sumatra, say

indicators.note: incorporating means taking in, so the country letter goes inside

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a land is a country or nation
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: One country absorbs Sweden and an Indonesian territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorporating' puts S inside ILAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumatra is a large Indonesian island, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Major road put down, securing thousands for old farm worker

parts.note: the M1 is a major British motorway, written MI

indicators.note: securing means holding firmly, so the letters go inside

parts.note: laid means put down
K and M both stand for a thousand

explanation.surface: A motorway is built that holds thousands of pounds for a farm labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London; the 1 doubles as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A milkmaid was a woman who milked cows on a farm in former times.

clue.text: Scheme to get board reduced

indicators.note: reduced means made shorter, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a plank is a length of board

explanation.surface: A plan to shrink the board of directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' looks like a committee; it is a piece of wood. 'reduced' takes the K off PLANK.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a scheme or programme of action.

clue.text: Misguidedly select it for ball

indicators.note: misguided means going wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly chooses an item for a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' suggests a dance or a sports ball, but it is anatomical slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Ball is an informal word for one of the male reproductive glands.

clue.text: Antipathetic to a bit of Scripture

parts.note: a verse is a numbered section of a chapter of the Bible

explanation.surface: Hostile to a passage from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is usually followed by 'to', which the clue uses as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Averse means strongly disinclined or opposed, the same as antipathetic.

clue.text: Dying to drop one missile

indicators.note: to drop means to let go of, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: perishing means dying
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone dying lets go of a thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to drop' removes I from PERISHING. Pershing was a US ballistic missile.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pershing was an American nuclear ballistic missile of the Cold War.

clue.text: Small 25 reported in hole

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a small island is an islet

explanation.surface: A tiny island is mentioned in a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 refers to the answer to 25-across, an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelet is a small reinforced hole for a lace or cord.
